Eye care in Clear Lake

What eye care looks like in Clear Lake

Clear Lake is a screen-heavy, sun-heavy, humid place to have eyes. The people who come through this door work long days on monitors at Johnson Space Center and the engineering firms along Bay Area Boulevard, spend weekends out on the water where the glare comes off the surface as well as the sky, and live through a Gulf Coast allergy season that leaves eyes dry, red and itchy for weeks at a stretch.

That shapes how we work. A long-hours screen worker needs the exam to look at focusing and comfort, not just the prescription. Someone out on the water most weekends needs a real conversation about polarized lenses and UV. Dry eye here is managed across a season rather than solved with one bottle of drops. And with a district full of Clear Creek ISD families, the exam calendar bunches hard in July and August, which is why the Saturday hours exist and why back-to-school exams get booked early.

Who we care for

From a four-year-old’s first exam to the checks that matter at seventy

Children from about age four or five, with a frame wall built for playground wear and first contact lens fittings around ten to twelve. Adults who need the prescription right and the eye health checked properly. Seniors watched for glaucoma, macular degeneration and cataract. Contact lens wearers, including hard-to-fit eyes. Patients with diabetes who need the annual retinal exam their physician asked for.

Plenty of the families here started as kids in this chair and now bring their own.

What brings people in

The problems Clear Lake patients come in with

Find the one that sounds like you. Each goes to the page that explains what we do about it.

Dry, gritty eyes Burning, watering or a constant sandy feeling — worse through Gulf Coast allergy season. Dry
A sudden red or sore eye Redness that came on quickly, with soreness, discharge or light sensitivity. A sudden red or sore eye
Pink eye Sticky, streaming, spreading through the household. Seen the same day where we can. Pink eye
Something in your eye Metal, grit or a splinter. Call us rather than an urgent care clinic without eye equipment. Something in your eye
New flashes or floaters A sudden shower of floaters or flashes of light needs looking at promptly. Call us straight away. New flashes or floaters
Family history of glaucoma Glaucoma is painless until it is not, so it is found on an exam rather than by symptoms. Family history of glaucoma
Diabetes and a retinal exam due The annual dilated retinal exam your physician asked for, reported back to them. Diabetes and a retinal exam due
A child’s prescription climbing every year Myopia that steps up at every visit can often be slowed rather than just re-corrected. A child’s prescription climbing every year
Blur at reading distance after forty Arms getting longer with the menu. Normal, and there are more options than readers. Blur at reading distance after forty
Contacts that stopped being comfortable Lenses that used to be fine and now dry out by mid-afternoon. Usually fixable. Contacts that stopped being comfortable

What your visit looks like

What happens when you come in

  • You call or book online. A real person answers the phone, not a menu, and will find you a time that works.
  • Paperwork before you arrive. Fill in your patient forms ahead of time so the visit starts on time.
  • Thirty unhurried minutes with the doctor. Not a slot compressed to fit more appointments into the day.
  • A real look at eye health, not just vision. The exam checks how your eyes are doing, not only what strength lens you need.
  • We go through what we found, in plain terms. What it means, what to watch, and what happens next.
  • The optical, if you need it. Frames and lenses chosen with your prescription in hand, with no pressure to buy here.
  • We keep your history. Same doctor next year, with your record in front of him.

What to bring to your visit

  • Your vision or medical insurance card, and we will check your benefits for you
  • Your current glasses, and your contact lens boxes or prescription if you wear them
  • A list of any medications you take
  • Sunglasses for the drive home, if your eyes are being dilated

Most vision and medical plans are accepted. If you are not sure whether yours is, call ahead and the front desk can usually tell you in a minute.

Insurance and what it costs

Bring your plan, we will handle the rest

We accept most vision and medical plans, including VSP, EyeMed, Superior Vision, Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Medicare, Cigna and Tricare. CareCredit financing is available and cash is welcome. Coverage varies by plan, so pricing is quote-based. Call and we will check your plan before you come in.

One thing worth knowing: a routine vision exam and a medical eye visit are often billed differently, and which one applies depends on why you are being seen. We will tell you which it is when you book.

How billing works

Why families come here

Forty-two years, one doctor, one office

Dr. Jerry Hyder, OD is a licensed therapeutic optometrist who has practiced in Clear Lake since 1984. Therapeutic means he treats eye disease rather than only writing prescriptions, so dry eye, glaucoma, diabetic eye disease and macular degeneration are managed here over time instead of referred out at the first sign.

This is a private practice, not a chain counter. You see the same doctor every visit, he has your history in front of him, and appointments run 30 minutes.

Common questions

Questions Clear Lake patients ask

Where are you located?

We are at 515 Bay Area Blvd #300, Houston, TX 77058, in Clear Lake — the same address since 1984. Parking is directly in front and the entrance is straight ahead from the lot, with no stairs. You can open us in Google Maps or call (281) 488-0066 and we will talk you in.

Are you open on Saturdays?

Yes. We are open Saturdays from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM, which is when a lot of the working and school-age appointments land. We are open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM, and closed Wednesdays and Sundays.

Do you take my insurance?

We accept most vision and medical plans, including VSP, EyeMed, Superior Vision, Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Medicare, Cigna and Tricare. CareCredit financing is available and cash is welcome. Call (281) 488-0066 and we will check your plan and your benefits before you come in, or read how billing works.

How much is an eye exam?

Pricing is quote-based, because what you pay depends on your plan, your benefits and what the visit turns out to involve. We do not publish figures we cannot stand behind. Call us with your insurance details and the front desk can usually tell you in a minute.

How old should my child be for a first exam?

We generally see children from about age four or five for a first full exam, earlier if you or your paediatrician have a specific concern. First contact lens fittings usually happen around ten to twelve. More on children’s eye care and pediatric eye exams.

Do you do LASIK?

We do not perform LASIK surgery here, but we handle the co-management around it — the evaluation beforehand and your follow-up care afterwards, with the surgery itself done by the surgeon. See LASIK co-management.

Are you a chain?

No. This is a private practice with one doctor, not a chain counter with a rota. Your eye doctor in Clear Lake is Dr. Jerry Hyder, OD, who has practiced here since 1984, you see him at every visit, and he has your history in front of him rather than reading it cold. More about the doctor.

How long does an appointment take?

A comprehensive exam runs about 30 minutes with the doctor, and it is not compressed to fit more appointments into the day. Allow extra time if you are choosing frames afterwards, or if your eyes are being dilated.

Can I be seen the same day for an eye emergency?

Yes. Call (281) 488-0066 as early in the day as you can. Outside our hours the after-hours line is (281) 217-1281, and for an eye injury or a sudden change in your vision, go to your nearest emergency room.

Do I need an appointment to look at frames?

No. Walk-ins are welcome if you want to browse the frame wall or have a pair adjusted. An appointment is only needed for an exam or a contact lens fitting.
